public_rationale: On 2024-07-28, Marcus called it his strong intuition that LLMs are never going to work reliably, at least not in the general form many people hoped for in 2023. The forecast has no deadline, so no finite date can confirm it. Under the contract, it would be contradicted early if independent evaluations showed a general-purpose LLM with near-zero hallucination and reasoning-error rates across broad tasks. The evidence in this record contains no such evaluation. Its only item is OpenAI's statement of 2025-09-05. That statement says GPT-5 has significantly fewer hallucinations but still has them, and that hallucinations remain a fundamental challenge for all large language models (e1). This is consistent with the forecast so far, but it does not settle it.
limitations: The record has one item, a developer's own statement from September 2025. It includes no broad independent evaluations.
The evidence does not cover anything after September 2025.
The claim leaves open what counts as 'working reliably' and whether tool-using reasoning models count as LLMs.

statement.excerpt: My strong intuition, having studied neural networks for over 30 years (they were part of my dissertation) and LLMs since 2019, is that LLMs are simply never going to work reliably, at least not in the general form that so many people last year seemed to be hoping.
statement.document_title: AlphaProof, AlphaGeometry, ChatGPT, and why the future of AI is neurosymbolic

our_interpretation: Plain reading: general-purpose LLMs (pure LLMs, not hybrid neurosymbolic systems) will never reach reliable performance across general tasks, meaning free of frequent hallucinations and reasoning errors, as many hoped in 2023.
'Never' has no deadline. The forecast can be contradicted early by a decisive event but cannot be confirmed by any finite date.
Whether reasoning models with tools still count as 'LLMs' is an open question in the claim itself.
criteria.support_condition: Cannot be finally confirmed at any finite date. Continued hallucination and error in leading LLMs is consistent with the claim but does not settle it.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Broad independent evaluations show a general-purpose LLM working reliably across diverse real-world tasks, for example near-zero hallucination and reasoning-error rates comparable to dependable software.
